title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree Signatures To The Qurans Heavenly Origin

questions.question: What two qualities of the Prophet are presented as signs that the Qur’an is truly from Allah?
questions.answer: His complete trust in the Qur’an and his unwavering commitment to it are both presented as clear signs.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Prophet’s state when revelation came to him?
questions.answer: It says he was in a special condition similar to sleep when revelation descended.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that his ordinary speech did not resemble the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It supports the idea that the Qur’an did not come from his own personal speech or style.

questions.question: What kind of knowledge did he convey through the Qur’an with full certainty?
questions.answer: He conveyed truths about major events from the past and the future, including matters beyond normal human access.

questions.question: How does the passage use the public scrutiny of his life as evidence?
questions.answer: It argues that even under intense observation, no deception or moral flaw was found in him.

questions.question: What does his steady affirmation of every statement of the Qur’an show?
questions.answer: It shows deep certainty and serves as a confirming sign of the Qur’an’s truth.

questions.question: According to the passage, how much of humanity is described as being drawn to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: About one-fifth of humanity, and even more broadly a large portion of mankind, is described that way.

questions.question: In what way are people said to respond to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They listen eagerly and attach themselves to it through religion because they seek truth.

questions.question: Besides human beings, what other creatures are said to gather around the Qur’an when it is recited?
questions.answer: Jinn, angels, and spiritual beings are said to gather around it.

questions.question: What main conclusion is drawn from the response of both humans and unseen beings to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Their response is presented as proof that the Qur’an is widely accepted and holds a very high rank.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the whole target passage?
questions.answer: The passage argues that the Prophet’s character and certainty, together with the broad acceptance of the Qur’an among creation, confirm that the Qur’an is true revelation.

questions.question: Who is described as the source of Islam and the one who explains the Qur’an?
questions.answer: The Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: How is his personal relationship with the Qur’an portrayed?
questions.answer: He is shown as honoring it more than anyone else and believing in it with total conviction.

questions.question: Why is his strong reverence for the Qur’an important in the argument?
questions.answer: It suggests that the person closest to its message recognized it as divine and not man-made.

questions.question: What contrast is made between the Qur’an and his other speech?
questions.answer: The passage says his other words were not like the Qur’an and did not come close to it.

questions.question: What does that contrast imply about the source of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It implies that the Qur’an came from beyond his own human ability.

questions.question: What kind of subjects did he report through the Qur’an confidently and without hesitation?
questions.answer: He reported hidden realities, especially major events related to the past and future.

questions.question: What inference does the passage draw from the absence of trickery in his life?
questions.answer: It treats that absence as evidence of honesty and reliability.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the “sharpest eyes” watching him?
questions.answer: To emphasize that even close critics and careful observers found no fraud in him.

questions.question: What role does the obedience of large numbers of people play in the argument?
questions.answer: Their attachment to the Qur’an is presented as a sign of its truth and power.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the unseen world to the Qur’an’s status?
questions.answer: It says unseen beings also respond to it reverently, which strengthens the claim that it is accepted beyond the human realm.

questions.question: What does the phrase about its “high position” point to?
questions.answer: It points to the Qur’an’s elevated standing and honored place among creation.

questions.question: If you put the two paragraphs together, what two broad kinds of evidence are used?
questions.answer: The first uses the Prophet’s truthfulness and certainty, and the second uses the acceptance of the Qur’an by many beings.

questions.question: What is one central claim made about the Prophet’s belief in the Qur’an?
questions.answer: His belief was stronger and more complete than anyone else’s.

questions.question: How does the passage treat his certainty about unseen matters?
questions.answer: It treats that certainty as meaningful evidence that he was conveying revelation rather than guessing.

questions.question: Why would the difference between the Qur’an and his normal speech matter for comprehension of the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Because it supports the claim that the Qur’an has a source distinct from ordinary human expression.

questions.question: What is the significance of saying that nothing shook his commitment to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It shows firmness, confidence, and complete assurance in its truth.

questions.question: What “stamp” does the first paragraph say these points provide?
questions.answer: They provide a confirming sign that the Qur’an is true revelation from Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the Prophet’s moral integrity?
questions.answer: It presents him as free of deceit and serious fault even under close examination.

questions.question: How does the passage describe humanity’s attitude toward the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It describes many people as attracted to it, attached to it, and eager to hear it.

questions.question: What motivation is given for people listening closely to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They are seeking truth.

questions.question: Which nonhuman groups are specifically named as responding to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Jinn, angels, and spirit beings.

questions.question: What does their response add that human response alone would not add?
questions.answer: It expands the evidence beyond the visible world and suggests a more universal recognition of the Qur’an.

questions.question: How would you summarize the cause-and-effect reasoning in the second paragraph?
questions.answer: Because many beings are drawn to the Qur’an and gather around its recitation, the passage concludes that it is greatly accepted and exalted.

questions.question: What overall lesson is a college student meant to take from this passage?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that both the Messenger’s integrity and the wide response to the Qur’an point to its divine truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Prophet’s confidence when speaking through the Qur’an about hidden matters?
questions.answer: It says he spoke with full assurance and no hesitation.

questions.question: Why is that confidence significant in the passage?
questions.answer: It is significant because he was speaking about matters beyond ordinary human knowledge.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by saying no fraud or defect was seen in him?
questions.answer: It implies that his message was not built on manipulation or dishonesty.

questions.question: How does the passage use the idea of constant observation?
questions.answer: It argues that sustained public scrutiny would have exposed falsehood if there had been any.

questions.question: What does his complete support of every statement of the Qur’an reveal about him?
questions.answer: It reveals absolute trust and submission to the message.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does this reveal about the Qur’an itself?
questions.answer: It reveals that the Qur’an is genuine revelation and truly from his Merciful Lord.

questions.question: How large is the human following described in the second paragraph?
questions.answer: It describes a fifth of humanity and even more broadly much of mankind.

questions.question: How are these people connected to the Qur’an in religious life?
questions.answer: They are tied to it through faith and attentive listening.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the reaction of unseen beings during recitation?
questions.answer: It says they gather around in a sincere and reverent way.

questions.question: What does that scene suggest about the Qur’an’s place in creation?
questions.answer: It suggests that the Qur’an has an honored place recognized across different kinds of beings.

questions.question: Which is emphasized more in the second paragraph: rejection or attraction?
questions.answer: Attraction is emphasized.

questions.question: What is the strongest shared theme running through both paragraphs?
questions.answer: Both stress recognition of the Qur’an’s truth, first by the Messenger and then by a vast range of beings.

questions.question: In the first paragraph, what personal evidence is given from the life of the Prophet?
questions.answer: His deep respect for the Qur’an, his certainty in it, his truthful character, and the difference between it and his own speech.

questions.question: How does the passage separate revelation from the Prophet’s personal authorship?
questions.answer: It points out that the Qur’an’s style did not match his ordinary speech and that he treated it as something received, not invented.

questions.question: What kinds of realities does the passage say he described through the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It says he described major realities connected to the unseen, especially from earlier times and what was to come.

questions.question: Why is honesty under close examination important to the argument?
questions.answer: Because a false claimant would likely be exposed when watched carefully over time.

questions.question: What conclusion does the first paragraph reach from all these points together?
questions.answer: It concludes that they confirm the Qur’an as divine revelation and true speech from Allah.

questions.question: What collective human response to the Qur’an is described next?
questions.answer: A very large part of humanity is said to be drawn to it and bound to it in faith.

questions.question: What inner attitude do these listeners have according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are eager and sincerely looking for truth.

questions.question: How does the passage broaden the audience beyond humanity?
questions.answer: It adds jinn, angels, and spirit beings as listeners and responders.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by calling these signs a “stamp”?
questions.answer: It means they function as confirming marks or proofs.

questions.question: What two “stamps” are presented in the target passage?
questions.answer: One is the Prophet’s certainty and integrity, and the other is the Qur’an’s broad acceptance among humans and unseen beings.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the passage’s message?
questions.answer: The message is that the Qur’an’s truth is confirmed both by the Messenger who received it and by the many beings who respond to it.

questions.question: What does the passage present as unusual about the Prophet’s speech in relation to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: His regular speech was different from the Qur’an and did not match its level or character.

questions.question: How does that detail help the reader understand the passage’s claim?
questions.answer: It supports the view that the Qur’an was not a product of his own verbal skill.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his reports of the past and future?
questions.answer: He communicated them confidently through the Qur’an as true realities.

questions.question: What personal quality is highlighted by the claim that no deception was detected in him?
questions.answer: Trustworthiness.

questions.question: How does his unshaken faith function as evidence in the passage?
questions.answer: It serves as a strong inner witness that he knew the Qur’an to be true.

questions.question: What relation between the Prophet and Allah is implied at the end of the first paragraph?
questions.answer: The Qur’an is presented as the blessed speech of his Merciful Creator.

questions.question: What scale of human acceptance is mentioned in the second paragraph?
questions.answer: It mentions acceptance by one-fifth of humanity and by a very large share of mankind overall.

questions.question: What does the passage say people do when they hear the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They listen with strong desire because they are seeking truth.

questions.question: Which unseen beings are named as responding to Qur’anic recitation?
questions.answer: Jinn, angels, and spirit beings.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the inclusion of both visible and unseen listeners?
questions.answer: The Qur’an’s influence is presented as universal rather than limited to one group.

questions.question: What judgment does the passage make about the Qur’an’s standing?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an holds a very lofty and honored rank.

questions.question: Looking at the target passage alone, what is the main argument being built?
questions.answer: The argument is that the Qur’an is true revelation, proven by the Messenger’s complete certainty and by its powerful acceptance among creation.
